A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SRPO, with matching core objectives, algorithms, and original experiments. All pages and appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic bandit experiments, LLaMA-7B summarization evaluations on TL;DR and XSum, an alpha ablation, and generated examples.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and adds LLaMA-3.1-8B preference-training experiments evaluated on Arena-Hard in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Appendix D introduces an average-log-likelihood variant of SRPO for variable-length responses, a limited loss adaptation. The core minimax objective, single-model design, sample losses, and Algorithm 1 are retained; the changes to theoretical equations are assessed under T1.

E1.justification: v4 adds ShareGPT-Vicuna supervised training, UltraFeedback preference training, and Arena-Hard evaluation. This substantially expands the empirical scope from summarization and synthetic bandits to general instruction following, while retaining the original coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix D evaluates RPO and SimPO alongside DPO and IPO, substantially broadening the comparison methods. SimPO is called SIMIPO in parts of the text but is identifiable through its citation and Table 1. LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct also becomes a reference opponent; the original comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: The added experiments use LLaMA-3.1-8B, one-epoch training stages, hyperparameter sweeps, and GPT-4o judging on 500 Arena-Hard prompts against LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct and individual baselines. These are new protocols, not replacements for the retained LLaMA-7B summarization experiments with GPT-4-0613 and 1,024 evaluation examples.

E4.justification: Figure 5 extends revision-depth analysis to Arena-Hard, showing that performance peaks after one revision and deteriorates with further revisions. The existing alpha ablation, synthetic behavior-policy shift experiment, and qualitative summarization cases are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations across 20 bootstrap evaluations, retaining the summarization procedure of resampling 512 observations from 1,024 examples. Figure 5 uses the same 20-bootstrap reporting practice. No new training-run counts, seeds, or significance-testing procedures are specified.

E6.justification: Original results in Figures 1–4 and the example summaries are unchanged. New Figure 5 reports roughly 56% SRPO win rate after one revision against LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, followed by declining performance. Table 1 adds direct comparisons, including 67.50% against DPO and 74.90% against SimPO at one revision. These are new-setting results, not improvements over comparable v1 measurements.

T1.justification: v4 Equations 4 and 14 change the generative-policy log-ratio signs from those in v1 Equations 11 and 10. This substantively alters the central population loss and preference identity, while the sample loss remains unchanged in v4 Equation 16, creating an inconsistency in the claimed derivation. Section 4.2.3 also reverses the alpha weights relative to Equations 2 and 17.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add explicit emphasis on inference-time error correction, and the abstract adds an Arena-Hard performance claim. The central contributions—joint self-improvement and generation, offline optimization, and independence from the behavior policy—remain the same.

C2.justification: Section 2 adds exposure bias and error accumulation as motivation, plus explanations that supervised self-correction may ignore the initial response or overfit refinement patterns. v4 drops v1's warning that behavior/base-model mismatch may undo SFT or pretraining. The finite-data qualification and concluding simple-task limitation remain.

D1.justification: Appendix D supplies a substantial new reproducibility recipe: dataset access references, TPU hardware, JAX/FLAX/OPTAX implementation, training schedules, batch sizes, method-specific beta values, and RPO's auxiliary-loss weight. Appendix C.3 also documents win-rate scoring. Existing summarization settings and prompt templates are retained.

R1.justification: v4 expands positioning around exposure bias, learned self-correction, and length-normalized alignment. Appendix A explicitly contrasts SRPO with Kumar et al.'s online self-correction and Pang et al.'s reasoning preference optimization, and adds newer alignment literature. This is a substantive expansion beyond relocating the existing related-work section.

P1.justification: The abstract and motivation are substantially rewritten, Section 4 is reorganized into a theorem, proof, and sample-loss derivation, and related work moves from the main text to Appendix A. Editorial regressions include duplicated bandit discussion and visible 'looseness=-1' text.

P2.justification: v4 changes the document-wide typography, headings, text layout, and placement of existing displays, including moving Figure 1 into the introduction and reflowing example tables. It adds Table 1 and Figure 5. The plotted content of Figures 1–4 is retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix D substantially strengthens empirical breadth beyond v1's summarization study and provides useful implementation details. However, the changed signs in v4's central population loss and preference identity conflict with the retained sample loss, weakening the theoretical justification; inconsistent mixture weights and duplicated prose add further problems. The substantial empirical gains and regression in the central mathematical presentation prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
